issue_context.title: Incomplete abs() docs and editor hints
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** v3.2.beta.custom_build.3a9284b56

**OS/device including version:** macOS Catalina 10.15.1 / MacBook Pro (Retina, 13-inch, Early 2015)

**Issue description:**

The argument of `abs()` can be either an `int` or `float`, and the function returns a value of the corresponding type.

```gdscript
var i = abs(1)
var f = abs(1.0)
assert(typeof(i) == TYPE_INT)
assert(typeof(f) == TYPE_REAL)
```

Although this behavior is partially mentioned in the function description, it only shows the `float` version of function signature in the documentation and editor hints:

![Screenshot of abs function in docs and editor hints](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/372476/70848856-2f9c3600-1eb2-11ea-85d7-9d423cf3167d.png)

So there are actually two `abs` functions, but currently it seems complicated to change the documentation. Because the two versions are made different by code under the same `GDScriptFunctions::Function::MATH_ABS` enum, and the signature in documentation is generated per `GDScriptFunctions::Function` enum.

p.s. The same goes for `sign()`, `min()`, `max()`, and `clamp()` too.
comments: Is it just required to modify the documentation for the said functions? I have trouble understanding why it would be complicated.

Ideally, there should be `float abs(s: float)` and `int abs(s: int)`, both in the documentation and editor hints.

I didn't look very deep into the source code. But from what I can tell, the documentation XML structures are generated/updated by code, probably the same code that provides the editor hint content. It seems that we can't simply add one new function definition to the XML and call it a day. (Maybe I overthinked it.)

To C++, there is only one `abs` function, identified by the `MATH_ABS` enum. The logically different signatures are implemented as hard coded type checks:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7d34d1a85f95edd1b29b8eb24cda49b355db2c3d/modules/gdscript/gdscript_functions.cpp#L270-L286

This seems to be a place that defines the signature for `abs` (I'm not sure). And it's one signature per enum.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7d34d1a85f95edd1b29b8eb24cda49b355db2c3d/modules/gdscript/gdscript_functions.cpp#L1626-L1629

So I think, to make the `abs` signature in the documenttion two, the code above should be changed first, which requires a better understanding of the code around.

---

A simpler fix might be making the signature `Variant abs(s: Variant)` and describe the valid types in the function description. Although I think it's less ideal.

review_comments: Fall-through branches should explicitly use `FALLTHROUGH;` macro (assuming that's what all the empty else branches are intended for).
I have made the suggested changes in the new commit
